clue.text: Gold mines essentially protecting corporation in Wall Street's fall?

indicators.note: the gold and centre letter sit on either side, shielding the next piece between them

parts.note: AU is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its centre, so the middle letter of mines is taken

parts.note: corporation is an old jokey word for a pot belly, a tum

explanation.surface: A gold-mining corporation shields itself as Wall Street tumbles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'protecting' sets the gold and the middle of 'mines' on either side of the belly. 'corporation' is old slang for a paunch. Americans, as on Wall Street, call autumn fall.
explanation.definitionFit: Fall is the American name for the season between summer and winter.

clue.text: Drive when hotel opens retreat

indicators.note: the hotel letter comes at the front of the drive word, opening it

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to ram is to drive or force in

explanation.surface: A motorist's drive ends as a hotel opens its doors as a getaway.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashram is a religious retreat or hermitage in India.

clue.text: Cook's device knocked over egg batter

indicators.note: knocked over means turned upside down, so in a down entry the word is read backwards

parts.note: a nit is the egg of a louse
in cricket an opener is a batter who goes in first

explanation.surface: A cook's equipment knocks over a bowl of egg batter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'batter' looks like the cook's mixture; it is a cricketer, the OPENER. 'knocked over' turns NIT to TIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen tool for cutting the lids off cans is something a cook uses.

clue.text: Sailor runs into sea near English river

indicators.note: into means the runs letter goes inside the sea word

parts.note: the main is a poetic word for the open sea
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A sailor runs into the sea close to an English river.
explanation.definitionFit: A mariner is a seaman, someone who sails ships.

clue.text: Notorious group of footballers visiting in Missouri, America

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside, so the footballers' letters are placed within the next words

parts.note: taken as written
MO is the postal abbreviation for the state of Missouri
the FA is the Football Association, which governs English football
US is short for the United States of America

explanation.surface: A notorious football team on tour in Missouri, in the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Infamous means well known for something bad, as notorious does.

clue.text: Flood survivor on board tall ship in seconds

indicators.note: seconds points to the second letter of each of the next words in turn

explanation.surface: A survivor of a flood climbs aboard a tall ship within seconds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in seconds' reads as 'very quickly' but asks for the second letters of 'on board tall ship'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the patriarch who built the ark lived through the great Flood.

clue.text: A Republican brings up what's owed

parts.note: to rear children is to bring them up

explanation.surface: A Republican politician raises the matter of outstanding debts.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrears are payments overdue, money still owed.

clue.text: Group of twenty crop up occasionally

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards
occasionally means taking only some letters, here every other one starting from the first

explanation.surface: A gathering of twenty people pops up every now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: Alternate letters of 'twenty crop' give TETCO; 'up' turns it round. 'Group of twenty' looks like the definition, but only 'Group' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: An octet is a group of eight, such as a band of eight musicians.

clue.text: Smartly trimmed tree somewhere near Cambridge

indicators.note: trimmed means the tree word has its last letter cut off

parts.note: a spruce is a conifer
Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, about 15 miles from Cambridge

explanation.surface: A neatly pruned tree stands in a spot close to Cambridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smartly trimmed' looks like one phrase, but 'trimmed' cuts the E from SPRUCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Spruce means neat and smart, so sprucely is in a smart way.

clue.text: Suspended railway line wanting fare

parts.note: something hung is suspended
RY is an abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A railway line closes, leaving would-be passengers short of a fare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fare' suggests a ticket price; here it is food.
explanation.definitionFit: Fare is food, so someone wanting it needs a meal.

clue.text: Wrote warrant on the counter after all banks ignored teller

indicators.note: counter suggests running counter, against the direction, so the letters are read backwards
the banks are each word's outer edges, so the first and last letters of both words are dropped

explanation.surface: A bank teller writes out a warrant at the counter after other banks turn him away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after all banks ignored' strips each word's first and last letters, and 'on the counter' reverses what is left. 'teller' and 'banks' suggest a bank, but a teller here tells a story.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrator is a storyteller, one who tells a tale.

clue.text: Playing biggest part in Michael Caine film

indicators.note: playing suggests letters at play, moving about into a new order
the lead role is the biggest part, and the lead of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Michael Caine takes the starring role in a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'biggest part' is the lead, so M, the first letter of 'Michael'; that M and CAINE are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinema means film as an art form or industry.

clue.text: One could do without this program having bad index

parts.note: an app is a computer program

indicators.note: bad suggests the word is spoilt, its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: A computer program with a broken index is something users manage without.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description: the body organ is said to be one people live without.
explanation.definitionFit: The vermiform appendix serves little purpose and can be removed, so a person manages without it.

clue.text: Freezing cold, getting curry to start

indicators.note: the curry comes first, at the start, with the cold letter after it

parts.note: a balti is a curry cooked in a metal bowl
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone frozen through warms up by ordering a curry as a starter.
explanation.walkthrough: BALTIC can mean very cold in British slang, from the Baltic Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: In informal British speech something bitterly cold is described by the northern sea's adjective.

clue.text: Daring cooking — serve on newspaper, wrapping small fish

indicators.note: cooking suggests the letters are being worked up into a new form
the newspaper's letters go round the small letter, as fish and chips come wrapped in paper

parts.note: the FT is the Financial Times
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing
an eel is a long snake-like fish

explanation.surface: A brave chef serves food on newspaper wrapped round small fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooking' rearranges SERVE ON as NERVESO, and 'wrapping' puts the newspaper round the small letter, as chip shops once wrapped fish in newsprint.
explanation.definitionFit: Courage under pressure is expressed with an idiom about iron-hard composure.

clue.text: Brains, say, of men with upcoming problem

parts.note: OR stands for Other Ranks, ordinary soldiers rather than officers

indicators.note: upcoming in a down entry means the letters climb, read from bottom to top

parts.note: a snag is a problem

explanation.surface: Something to do with men's brains and an approaching difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: The brain is one of the body's organs; 'say' marks it as an example.

clue.text: Cast of Grease get chocolate treat?

indicators.note: cast can mean thrown about, so these letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: The cast of the musical Grease receive chocolates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like the actors in the musical; it is the anagram signal. The question mark shows the answer is only one kind of chocolate treat.
explanation.definitionFit: Hollow chocolate eggs are given as gifts at the spring festival.

clue.text: Escort from the premises the man keeping us from utter defeat

indicators.note: the man keeps us from the defeat, standing between the two words

parts.note: taken as written
a rout is a complete defeat
he means the man

explanation.surface: A man shows us the door so we avoid total humiliation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping us from' means separating: the man stands between the two words, as a protector would.
explanation.definitionFit: To show someone to the door is to escort them off the premises.

clue.text: What's on in the theatre?

parts.note: reads as a question about current plays, but the theatre is the operating theatre and what is on is what the surgeons wear

explanation.definitionFit: Surgeons put on special robes before operating in the operating theatre.

clue.text: Cover central ingredient of radon in lead casing

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the lead word encloses the radon letter like a case

parts.note: a clue is a lead in a detective's inquiry

indicators.note: central points to the middle letter of radon

explanation.surface: Radon is shielded inside a lead case for protection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' reads as the metal; it is a clue, CLUE, which encases D, the centre of 'radon'.
explanation.definitionFit: To cover a topic is to deal with it, to take it in.

clue.text: Something ref uses in game with Pelé in second half

parts.note: whist is a card game

indicators.note: the second half of the footballer's name, its last two letters

explanation.surface: A football match where Pelé plays only after half-time, and the referee gets busy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' and 'second half' suggest football; the game is a card game, and the half is of Pelé's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A football referee blows a small metal pipe to stop play.

clue.text: Endeavour to cut tree back, revealing shrub

indicators.note: back means the whole result is read in reverse
the endeavour word cuts into the tree word, sitting inside it

parts.note: the elm is a tree
to try is to endeavour

explanation.surface: Someone tries to cut a tree back and finds a bush underneath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cut' sets the endeavour inside the tree, giving ELTRYM, which 'back' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: The evergreen with fragrant white flowers sacred to Venus is a bush.

clue.text: Gene Vincent Covers Show

indicators.note: covers means the outside words hold the answer within them

explanation.surface: A headline: the rock singer Gene Vincent's songs, sung by others, get their own show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Covers' looks like cover versions of Gene Vincent's songs; it says his name holds the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To evince a feeling is to show it plainly.

clue.text: Maybe 14 Across papers on Isle of Man

parts.note: ID is identification, papers that prove who you are

explanation.surface: Perhaps someone's identity papers are stamped on the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixed expression whose meaning is not the sum of its words, like that one, is a turn of phrase.

clue.text: I depend on hospital department completely

indicators.note: in an across answer, on means placed after, so the I-depend piece follows the hospital department

parts.note: ENT is ear, nose and throat, a hospital department
to rely is to depend

explanation.surface: A patient says they depend on a hospital department.
explanation.definitionFit: Entirely means wholly, through and through.

clue.text: POTUS using drug to knock out politician for real

indicators.note: the drug's letter knocks the politician's letters out of their place, replacing them

parts.note: POTUS is the President of the United States, here Donald Trump
an MP is a Member of Parliament
E is ecstasy

explanation.surface: The US President takes drugs to defeat a politician, and means it.
explanation.walkthrough: Replace MP in TRUMP with E to get TRUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something true is genuine, actual.

clue.text: Report of passing out, treated with air by …

indicators.note: treated suggests the letters are processed and come out reworked

explanation.surface: A medical report: someone fainted and was given air by medics, as the next clue continues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passing out' reads as fainting; 'passing' is death and 'out' is anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper's notice of a death reports someone's passing.

clue.text: … medics at our care home — attendant finally finding way

indicators.note: finally points to the final letter of each word in turn

explanation.surface: Medics at a care home and an attendant find a way to help.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue continues 26 Across; 'finally' takes the last letter of each word from 'medics' to 'attendant'.
explanation.definitionFit: A street is a road, a public way.

clue.text: Meddled with tide — regularly taking measure of current

indicators.note: taking means those letters take in, enclose, the next piece
regularly means taking every other letter of tide, the first and third

parts.note: the ampere is the unit of electric current

explanation.surface: Someone tampered with the tide, regularly measuring its current.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' looks like the tide's flow; it is electrical.
explanation.definitionFit: To tamper is to meddle, to interfere improperly.

clue.text: Jungle Fever striking famous psychologist's class

indicators.note: striking means hitting out, so the psychologist's name is struck from the word

parts.note: Carl Jung was a famous Swiss psychologist
ague is an old word for a malarial fever

explanation.surface: A film title, Jungle Fever, hits a famous psychologist's lecture class.
explanation.walkthrough: Strike JUNG from 'Jungle' to leave LE, then add AGUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A league is a class or level, as in 'not in the same league'.
